# Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — Final Linear MILP

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $I$ | set of trains, indexed $i, j$ |
| $S$ | set of segments (blocks), indexed $s$ |
| $T$ | set of time steps, indexed $t$ |
| $K$ | set of discrete speed levels, indexed $k$ |
| $D = \{0,1\}$ | directions: $0$ = normal, $1$ = opposite |
| $ST_i$ | ordered set of stations on train $i$'s route |
| $S_i \subseteq S$ | ordered set of segments traversed by train $i$ |
| $T_i \subseteq T$ | time steps relevant to train $i$ |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $L_s$ | length of segment $s$ |
| $v_k$ | speed of level $k$ |
| $e_k$ | energy consumption rate at speed level $k$ (per unit time) |
| $v_{\max}$ | maximum allowed speed |
| $a_{\max}, d_{\max}$ | max acceleration / deceleration |
| $h$ | minimum same-direction headway time |
| $h_{\text{opp}}$ | minimum opposite-direction separation time |
| $dw^{\min}_i, dw^{\max}_i$ | min/max dwell time of train $i$ |
| $r^{\min}_{i,s}, r^{\max}_{i,s}$ | min/max running time of train $i$ on segment $s$ |
| $t_{\text{start}}, t_{\text{end}}$ | disruption window bounds on blocked segment $s^*$ |
| $s^*$ | blocked segment |
| $w_{\text{delay}}, w_{\text{cancel}}, w_{\text{energy}}$ | objective weights |
| $P_i$ | number of passengers (weight) on train $i$ |
| $a^{\text{sched}}_{i,\text{dest}}$ | scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at destination |
| $M$ | large constant |
| $T_{\text{horizon}}$ | end of planning horizon |
| $dt$ | time-step length |

## 3. Decision Variables

**Routing / Cancellation**
- $y_{i,s,d} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses direction $d$ on segment $s$
- $z_i \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is cancelled

**Timing**
- $a_{i,st} \ge 0$: arrival time of train $i$ at station $st$
- $dep_{i,st} \ge 0$: departure time of train $i$ from station $st$
- $en_{i,s} \ge 0$: entry time of train $i$ into segment $s$
- $ex_{i,s} \ge 0$: exit time of train $i$ from segment $s$

**Speed Profile**
- $x_{i,s,t,k} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is on segment $s$ at time $t$ at speed level $k$
- $v_{i,t} \ge 0$: speed of train $i$ at time $t$
- $acc_{i,t} \ge 0$: acceleration of train $i$ at time $t$
- $dec_{i,t} \ge 0$: deceleration of train $i$ at time $t$

**Ordering / Headway**
- $u_{i,j,s,d} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $s$ in direction $d$
- $w_{i,j,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ enters segment $s$ before train $j$ (any direction)

**Disruption Overlap**
- $\theta_{i,s^*} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$'s traversal of $s^*$ overlaps $[t_{\text{start}}, t_{\text{end}}]$

**Objective Auxiliaries**
- $E_i \ge 0$: energy consumption of train $i$
- $\text{delay}_i \ge 0$: positive delay of train $i$ at destination

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; w_{\text{delay}} \sum_{i \in I} P_i \,\text{delay}_i
\;+\; w_{\text{cancel}} \sum_{i \in I} z_i
\;+\; w_{\text{energy}} \sum_{i \in I} E_i
$$

## 5. Constraints

**(C1) Route / track selection**
$$
y_{i,s,0} + y_{i,s,1} = 1 - z_i \qquad \forall i \in I,\; s \in S_i
$$

**(C2) Disruption — linearized overlap and track unavailability**
$$
en_{i,s^*} \le t_{\text{end}} + M(1 - \theta_{i,s^*}) \tag{C2a}
$$
$$
ex_{i,s^*} \ge t_{\text{start}} - M(1 - \theta_{i,s^*}) \tag{C2b}
$$
$$
\theta_{i,s^*} \le 1 - z_i \tag{C2c}
$$
$$
y_{i,s^*,0} \le 1 - \theta_{i,s^*} \qquad \forall i \in I \tag{C2d}
$$

**(C3) Segment–time–speed linking**
$$
\sum_{s \in S_i} \sum_{k \in K} x_{i,s,t,k} = 1 - z_i \qquad \forall i \in I,\; t \in T_i \tag{C3a}
$$
$$
\sum_{t \in T_i} \sum_{k \in K} x_{i,s,t,k} \ge 1 - z_i - M(1 - y_{i,s,0} - y_{i,s,1}) \qquad \forall i, s \in S_i \tag{C3b}
$$
$$
v_{i,t} = \sum_{s \in S_i} \sum_{k \in K} v_k \, x_{i,s,t,k} \qquad \forall i \in I,\; t \in T_i \tag{C3c}
$$

**(C4) Speed dynamics (bounded acceleration/deceleration)**
$$
v_{i,t+1} - v_{i,t} = acc_{i,t} - dec_{i,t} \qquad \forall i \in I,\; t \in T_i \tag{C4a}
$$
$$
acc_{i,t} \le a_{\max} \cdot dt \qquad \forall i, t \tag{C4b}
$$
$$
dec_{i,t} \le d_{\max} \cdot dt \qquad \forall i, t \tag{C4c}
$$
$$
v_{i,t} \le v_{\max} \qquad \forall i, t \tag{C4d}
$$

**(C5) Segment traversal consistency (no "jumping")**
$$
t \cdot dt \ge en_{i,s} - M(1 - x_{i,s,t,k}) \qquad \forall i, s, t, k \tag{C5a}
$$
$$
t \cdot dt \le ex_{i,s} + M(1 - x_{i,s,t,k}) \qquad \forall i, s, t, k \tag{C5b}
$$
$$
v_k \cdot dt \le L_s + M(1 - x_{i,s,t,k}) \qquad \forall i, s, t, k \tag{C5c}
$$

**(C6) Running time on each segment**
$$
r^{\min}_{i,s} \le ex_{i,s} - en_{i,s} \le r^{\max}_{i,s} \qquad \forall i, s \in S_i \tag{C6}
$$

**(C7) Arrival / departure linkage and dwell times**
$$
a_{i,st+1} = ex_{i,s} \qquad \forall i, s \in S_i \tag{C7a}
$$
$$
dep_{i,st} = en_{i,s} \qquad \forall i, s \in S_i \tag{C7b}
$$
$$
dep_{i,st} - a_{i,st} \ge dw^{\min}_i - M z_i \qquad \forall i, st \in ST_i \tag{C7c}
$$
$$
dep_{i,st} - a_{i,st} \le dw^{\max}_i + M z_i \qquad \forall i, st \in ST_i \tag{C7d}
$$

**(C8) Same-direction headway (ordering)**
$$
u_{i,j,s,d} + u_{j,i,s,d} \ge y_{i,s,d} + y_{j,s,d} - 1 \qquad \forall i \ne j, s, d \tag{C8a}
$$
$$
u_{i,j,s,d} + u_{j,i,s,d} \le 1 \qquad \forall i \ne j, s, d \tag{C8b}
$$
$$
en_{j,s} \ge ex_{i,s} + h - M(1 - u_{i,j,s,d}) \qquad \forall i \ne j, s, d \tag{C8c}
$$

**(C9) Bidirectional conflict (opposite directions on shared track)**
$$
en_{j,s} \ge ex_{i,s} + h_{\text{opp}} - M(1 - w_{i,j,s}) \qquad \forall i \ne j, s \tag{C9a}
$$
$$
en_{i,s} \ge ex_{j,s} + h_{\text{opp}} - M \, w_{i,j,s} \qquad \forall i \ne j, s \tag{C9b}
$$
$$
w_{i,j,s} + w_{j,i,s} \ge y_{i,s,0} + y_{j,s,1} - 1 \qquad \forall i \ne j, s \tag{C9c}
$$
$$
w_{i,j,s} + w_{j,i,s} \ge y_{i,s,1} + y_{j,s,0} - 1 \qquad \forall i \ne j, s \tag{C9d}
$$

**(C10) No overtaking within a segment**
$$
ex_{i,s} \le ex_{j,s} + M(1 - w_{i,j,s}) \qquad \forall i \ne j, s \tag{C10}
$$

**(C11) Cancellation consistency**
$$
a_{i,st} \le M(1 - z_i) + T_{\text{horizon}} \qquad \forall i, st \tag{C11a}
$$
$$
en_{i,s} \le M(1 - z_i) + T_{\text{horizon}} \qquad \forall i, s \tag{C11b}
$$
$$
ex_{i,s} \le M(1 - z_i) + T_{\text{horizon}} \qquad \forall i, s \tag{C11c}
$$

**(C12) Energy consumption**
$$
E_i = \sum_{s \in S_i} \sum_{t \in T_i} \sum_{k \in K} e_k \cdot x_{i,s,t,k} \cdot dt \qquad \forall i \in I \tag{C12}
$$

**(C13) Delay linearization**
$$
\text{delay}_i \ge a_{i,\text{dest}_i} - a^{\text{sched}}_{i,\text{dest}_i} - M z_i \qquad \forall i \in I \tag{C13a}
$$
$$
\text{delay}_i \ge 0 \qquad \forall i \in I \tag{C13b}
$$

**(C14) Domain constraints**
$$
x_{i,s,t,k},\; y_{i,s,d},\; z_i,\; u_{i,j,s,d},\; w_{i,j,s},\; \theta_{i,s^*} \in \{0,1\}
$$
$$
a_{i,st},\; dep_{i,st},\; en_{i,s},\; ex_{i,s},\; v_{i,t},\; acc_{i,t},\; dec_{i,t},\; E_i,\; \text{delay}_i \ge 0
$$

## 6. Model Summary

The model integrates **train rescheduling (TRP)** and **speed management (TSMP)** into a single MILP for a partial segment blockage disruption. It simultaneously decides:

- **Retiming** — via $a_{i,st}, dep_{i,st}, en_{i,s}, ex_{i,s}$
- **Reordering** — via $u_{i,j,s,d}$ (same direction) and $w_{i,j,s}$ (bidirectional)
- **Rerouting** — via $y_{i,s,d}$, forced onto the opposite track during the disruption window by (C2d)
- **Cancellation** — via $z_i$
- **Speed profiles** — via $x_{i,s,t,k}, v_{i,t}, acc_{i,t}, dec_{i,t}$

**Key linearization techniques used:**
- Big-M disjunctions for disruption overlap (C2), headway (C8), bidirectional conflict (C9), and no-overtaking (C10)
- Auxiliary variable for delay (C13) to avoid the non-linear $\max(0,\cdot)$
- Discrete speed levels to keep energy (C12) linear
- Segment–time linking (C3, C5) to align the timetable with the speed profile

**Assumptions (marked):** time discretization on grid $dt$; piecewise-constant speed per segment/time step; linear acceleration/deceleration approximation; rerouting changes only track direction, not station sequence; known fixed disruption window; finite discrete speed set.

The formulation is fully linear and solvable with standard MILP solvers (Gurobi, CPLEX); for large networks, decomposition or rolling-horizon methods are recommended.

# MILP Model: Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

Below is the complete linear model derived from the generated code, expressed as equations.

---

## Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $Seg$ | Set of segments between consecutive stations, indexed by $g$ (segment $g$ connects station $g$ and $g+1$) |
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i$ |
| $D \subseteq Seg$ | Set of disruption-affected segments |
| $K$ | Set of discrete speed-profile options, indexed by $k$ |
| $P$ | Set of discretization points along a segment, indexed by $p = 0,\dots,P_{\max}$ |
| $TP$ | Set of ordered train pairs $(i,j)$ with $i<j$ |

---

## Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $t0_i$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ from its origin |
| $dwell_i$ | Minimum dwell time of train $i$ |
| $r_{i,g,k}$ | Running time of train $i$ on segment $g$ under profile $k$ |
| $e_{i,g,k}$ | Energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $g$ under profile $k$ |
| $L_g$ | Length of segment $g$ |
| $W^{start}_g, W^{end}_g$ | Start/end of disruption window on affected segment $g \in D$ |
| $a^{sched}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $v_{\max}$ | Maximum train speed |
| $a_{\max}$ | Maximum acceleration magnitude |
| $M$ | Large positive constant (big-M) |
| $C_{delay}, C_{energy}, C_{cancel}, C_{dev}$ | Cost coefficients |
| $headway$ | Minimum safety headway time |
| $dt$ | Discretization time step |
| $dir(i)$ | Direction of train $i$ (up/down) |
| $dest(i)$ | Destination station of train $i$ |

---

## Decision Variables

| Symbol | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| $x_{i,g,k}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ uses speed profile $k$ on segment $g$ |
| $a_{i,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $dep_{i,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $y_{i,g}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ is rerouted on segment $g$ |
| $z_{i,j,g}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $g$ |
| $u_{i,g}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $g$ during the disruption window |
| $cancel_i$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $pos_{i,g,p}$ | $\geq 0$ | Position of train $i$ on segment $g$ at point $p$ |
| $vel_{i,g,p}$ | $\geq 0$ | Speed of train $i$ on segment $g$ at point $p$ |
| $acc_{i,g,p}$ | Free | Acceleration of train $i$ on segment $g$ at point $p$ |
| $delay_i$ | $\geq 0$ | Arrival delay of train $i$ at destination |
| $t^{start}_{i,g}$ | $\geq 0$ | Time train $i$ enters segment $g$ |
| $t^{end}_{i,g}$ | $\geq 0$ | Time train $i$ leaves segment $g$ |
| $dev_{i,s}$ | $\geq 0$ | Absolute deviation of arrival time from schedule |

---

## Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = \sum_{i \in T} C_{delay}\, delay_i
+ \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{g \in Seg}\sum_{k \in K} C_{energy}\, e_{i,g,k}\, x_{i,g,k}
+ \sum_{i \in T} C_{cancel}\, cancel_i
+ \sum_{i \in T}\sum_{s \in S} C_{dev}\, dev_{i,s}
$$

---

## Constraints

**(1) Speed profile selection** — exactly one profile per train per segment (unless cancelled):
$$
\sum_{k \in K} x_{i,g,k} = 1 - cancel_i \qquad \forall i \in T,\; g \in Seg
$$

**(2) Running time consistency:**
$$
t^{end}_{i,g} - t^{start}_{i,g} = \sum_{k \in K} r_{i,g,k}\, x_{i,g,k} \qquad \forall i \in T,\; g \in Seg
$$

**(3) Arrival/departure linkage:**
$$
a_{i,g+1} = t^{end}_{i,g} \qquad \forall i \in T,\; g \in Seg
$$
$$
dep_{i,g} = t^{start}_{i,g} \qquad \forall i \in T,\; g \in Seg
$$
$$
dep_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \geq dwell_i\,(1 - cancel_i) \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

**(4) Segment traversal timing:**
$$
t^{start}_{i,g} \geq dep_{i,g} \qquad \forall i \in T,\; g \in Seg
$$
$$
t^{end}_{i,g} \leq a_{i,g+1} \qquad \forall i \in T,\; g \in Seg
$$

**(5) Disruption window / blockage** (for $g \in D$):
$$
t^{start}_{i,g} \geq W^{end}_g - M\,(1 - u_{i,g})
$$
$$
t^{end}_{i,g} \leq W^{start}_g + M\,u_{i,g}
$$
$$
u_{i,g} \leq y_{i,g}
$$

**(6) Rerouting only allowed on affected segments:**
$$
y_{i,g} = 0 \qquad \forall i \in T,\; g \notin D
$$

**(7) Headway / ordering** (for all train pairs $(i,j) \in TP$, all $g$):
$$
t^{start}_{j,g} \geq t^{end}_{i,g} + headway - M\,(1 - z_{i,j,g})
$$
$$
t^{start}_{i,g} \geq t^{end}_{j,g} + headway - M\,z_{i,j,g}
$$

**(8) Rerouting conflict** — opposite-direction trains cannot both reroute on the same affected segment (for $g \in D$, $dir(i) \neq dir(j)$):
$$
y_{i,g} + y_{j,g} \leq 1
$$

**(9) Discretized train dynamics** (for $p < P_{\max}$):
$$
pos_{i,g,p+1} = pos_{i,g,p} + vel_{i,g,p}\,dt + \tfrac{1}{2}\,acc_{i,g,p}\,dt^2
$$
$$
vel_{i,g,p+1} = vel_{i,g,p} + acc_{i,g,p}\,dt
$$
$$
-a_{\max} \leq acc_{i,g,p} \leq a_{\max}
$$
$$
0 \leq vel_{i,g,p} \leq v_{\max}
$$
$$
pos_{i,g,0} = 0, \qquad pos_{i,g,P_{\max}} = L_g\,(1 - cancel_i)
$$

**(10) Distance consistency with selected profile:**
$$
\sum_{p \in P} vel_{i,g,p}\,dt = L_g \sum_{k \in K} x_{i,g,k} \qquad \forall i \in T,\; g \in Seg
$$

**(11) Delay definition:**
$$
delay_i \geq a_{i,dest(i)} - a^{sched}_{i,dest(i)} \qquad \forall i \in T
$$

**(12) Cancellation linkage:**
$$
a_{i,s} \leq M\,(1 - cancel_i) \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$
$$
dep_{i,s} \leq M\,(1 - cancel_i) \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

**(13) Time deviation linearization:**
$$
dev_{i,s} \geq a_{i,s} - a^{sched}_{i,s} \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$
$$
dev_{i,s} \geq a^{sched}_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \qquad \forall i \in T,\; s \in S
$$

**(14) Variable domains:**
$$
x_{i,g,k},\, y_{i,g},\, z_{i,j,g},\, u_{i,g},\, cancel_i \in \{0,1\}
$$
$$
a_{i,s},\, dep_{i,s},\, t^{start}_{i,g},\, t^{end}_{i,g},\, delay_i,\, dev_{i,s},\, pos_{i,g,p},\, vel_{i,g,p} \geq 0
$$
$$
acc_{i,g,p} \in \mathbb{R}
$$

---

## Assumptions (marked)

- **A1:** The line is a single-track-per-direction railway; rerouting uses the opposite track.
- **A2:** The disruption is a partial blockage on a subset of segments during a known time window.
- **A3:** Speed profiles are discretized into a finite set of options per segment.
- **A4:** Train dynamics are linearized via a small time step $dt$.
- **A5:** Dwell times are lower-bounded; no upper bound is imposed.
- **A6:** Cancellation is allowed but penalized.
- **A7:** Headway and occupation times are deterministic and known.
- **A8:** All trains have fixed origin, destination, and direction.
- **A9:** Energy consumption per profile option is precomputed.
- **A10:** The objective is a weighted sum of delay, energy, cancellation, and schedule-deviation costs.

---

**Note on complexity:** The model contains $O(|T|^2 \cdot |Seg|)$ binary ordering variables, so for realistic network sizes a decomposition-based solution method (as described in the paper) is recommended.

# Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)
## Complete MILP Formulation

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of segments (blocks), indexed by $s$, ordered along the line |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of discrete speed levels, indexed by $k$ |
| $\mathcal{S}_d \subseteq \mathcal{S}$ | Set of disrupted (blocked) segments |
| $\mathcal{T}_d \subseteq \mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains whose direction is blocked on $\mathcal{S}_d$ |
| $\mathcal{P}_s$ | Set of ordered train pairs $(t_1, t_2)$ that may conflict on segment $s$ |

Each train $t$ has a direction $d(t) \in \{\text{up}, \text{down}\}$.

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $L_s$ | Length of segment $s$ [km] |
| $v_k$ | Speed of level $k$ [km/h] |
| $e_k$ | Energy consumption rate at speed level $k$ (assumed $\propto v_k^2$) |
| $a_{\max}, b_{\max}$ | Maximum acceleration / deceleration |
| $t^{\min}_s$ | Minimum running time on segment $s$ |
| $\text{dwell}_{\min}, \text{dwell}_{\max}$ | Min/max dwell time at stations |
| $h$ | Minimum safety headway |
| $A^{\text{sch}}_t, D^{\text{sch}}_t$ | Nominal scheduled arrival / departure times of train $t$ |
| $t_{\text{start}}, t_{\text{end}}$ | Disruption time window boundaries |
| $M$ | Large constant (big-M) |
| $w_{\text{delay}}, w_{\text{energy}}$ | Objective weights |
| $s_{\text{last}}$ | Index of the last segment (terminal station) |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $x_{t,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ reroutes onto opposite track on segment $s$ |
| $y_{t_1,t_2,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t_1$ precedes train $t_2$ on segment $s$ |
| $\text{arr}_{t,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Arrival time of train $t$ at start of segment $s$ |
| $\text{dep}_{t,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Departure time of train $t$ from start of segment $s$ |
| $\text{dwell}_{t,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Dwell time of train $t$ at station before segment $s$ |
| $v^{\text{sel}}_{t,s,k}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $t$ uses speed level $k$ on segment $s$ |
| $\text{run}_{t,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Running time of train $t$ on segment $s$ |
| $\text{delay}_t$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Delay of train $t$ relative to nominal schedule |
| $\text{energy}_{t,s}$ | $\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ | Energy consumed by train $t$ on segment $s$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = w_{\text{delay}} \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \text{delay}_t \;+\; w_{\text{energy}} \sum_{t \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \text{energy}_{t,s}
$$

Minimizes a weighted sum of total train delay and total traction energy consumption.

---

## 5. Constraints

### (C1) Speed selection — exactly one level per train-segment
$$
\sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} v^{\text{sel}}_{t,s,k} = 1 \qquad \forall\, t \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

### (C2) Running time linked to selected speed
$$
\text{run}_{t,s} = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \frac{L_s}{v_k}\, v^{\text{sel}}_{t,s,k} \qquad \forall\, t \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

### (C3) Energy linked to selected speed
$$
\text{energy}_{t,s} = \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} e_k \cdot \frac{L_s}{v_k}\, v^{\text{sel}}_{t,s,k} \qquad \forall\, t \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

### (C4) Dwell time bounds
$$
\text{dwell}_{\min} \le \text{dwell}_{t,s} \le \text{dwell}_{\max} \qquad \forall\, t \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

### (C5) Departure = arrival + dwell
$$
\text{dep}_{t,s} = \text{arr}_{t,s} + \text{dwell}_{t,s} \qquad \forall\, t \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

### (C6) Time propagation across segments
$$
\text{arr}_{t,s+1} = \text{dep}_{t,s} + \text{run}_{t,s} \qquad \forall\, t \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}\setminus\{s_{\text{last}}\}
$$

### (C7) Delay definition (relative to nominal arrival at terminal)
$$
\text{delay}_t \ge \text{arr}_{t,s_{\text{last}}} - A^{\text{sch}}_t \qquad \forall\, t \in \mathcal{T}
$$
$$
\text{delay}_t \ge 0 \qquad \forall\, t \in \mathcal{T}
$$

### (C8) Disruption handling — reroute or wait until disruption ends
For $s \in \mathcal{S}_d$ and $t \in \mathcal{T}_d$:
$$
\text{dep}_{t,s} \ge t_{\text{end}} - M\, x_{t,s}
$$
*Interpretation:* if $x_{t,s}=0$ (no reroute), then $\text{dep}_{t,s} \ge t_{\text{end}}$ (train waits until the disruption window closes); if $x_{t,s}=1$, the constraint is relaxed.

### (C9) Rerouting only permitted on disrupted segments
$$
x_{t,s} = 0 \qquad \forall\, t \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}\setminus\mathcal{S}_d
$$

### (C10) Bidirectional conflict on shared track (opposite-direction trains)
For each segment $s$ and each ordered pair $(t_1,t_2) \in \mathcal{P}_s$ that may share the physical track (i.e., at least one is rerouted):
$$
\text{dep}_{t_2,s} \ge \text{dep}_{t_1,s} + h - M\,(1 - y_{t_1,t_2,s})
$$
$$
\text{dep}_{t_1,s} \ge \text{dep}_{t_2,s} + h - M\, y_{t_1,t_2,s}
$$

### (C11) Same-direction headway
For trains $t_1, t_2$ with $d(t_1) = d(t_2)$ on the same track of segment $s$:
$$
\text{dep}_{t_2,s} \ge \text{dep}_{t_1,s} + h - M\,(1 - y_{t_1,t_2,s})
$$
$$
\text{dep}_{t_1,s} \ge \text{dep}_{t_2,s} + h - M\, y_{t_1,t_2,s}
$$

### (C12) Minimum running time
$$
\text{run}_{t,s} \ge t^{\min}_s \qquad \forall\, t \in \mathcal{T},\; s \in \mathcal{S}
$$

### (C13) Acceleration / deceleration feasibility (linearized)
For consecutive segments $s, s+1$ and speed levels $k, k'$:
$$
v_{k'} - v_k \le a_{\max} \cdot \text{run}_{t,s} + M\,(2 - v^{\text{sel}}_{t,s,k} - v^{\text{sel}}_{t,s+1,k'})
$$
$$
v_k - v_{k'} \le b_{\max} \cdot \text{run}_{t,s} + M\,(2 - v^{\text{sel}}_{t,s,k} - v^{\text{sel}}_{t,s+1,k'})
$$
These constraints activate only when $v^{\text{sel}}_{t,s,k} = v^{\text{sel}}_{t,s+1,k'} = 1$.

### (C14) Variable domains
$$
x_{t,s},\; y_{t_1,t_2,s},\; v^{\text{sel}}_{t,s,k} \in \{0,1\}
$$
$$
\text{arr}_{t,s},\; \text{dep}_{t,s},\; \text{dwell}_{t,s},\; \text{run}_{t,s},\; \text{delay}_t,\; \text{energy}_{t,s} \ge 0
$$

---

## 6. Model Interpretation

| Component | Role |
|-----------|------|
| **Retiming** | $\text{arr}_{t,s}, \text{dep}_{t,s}, \text{dwell}_{t,s}$ shift trains in time |
| **Reordering** | $y_{t_1,t_2,s}$ decides which train goes first on a segment |
| **Rerouting** | $x_{t,s}$ moves a train onto the opposite track during the disruption |
| **Speed management** | $v^{\text{sel}}_{t,s,k}$ selects a discrete speed; $\text{run}_{t,s}, \text{energy}_{t,s}$ follow |
| **Safety** | Headway constraints (C10–C11) prevent conflicts on shared track |
| **Disruption logic** | Big-M in (C8) forces either reroute or wait past $t_{\text{end}}$ |
| **Physics** | (C12)–(C13) enforce minimum run time and accel/decel limits |

---

## 7. Key Modeling Assumptions

1. **Discrete speed levels** — continuous speed profiles are approximated by $|\mathcal{K}|$ levels.
2. **Energy $\propto v_k^2$** — tractive energy rate scales quadratically with speed (captured via precomputed $e_k$).
3. **Constant accel/decel bounds** — linearized via big-M on consecutive-segment speed transitions.
4. **Single-track-per-direction** — the opposite track is normally used by the other direction; rerouting creates bidirectional sharing.
5. **Big-M validity** — $M$ chosen large enough to deactivate constraints when binaries are 0.
6. **Pairwise ordering** — $y$ variables defined only for train pairs that can physically conflict on a segment.

---

## 8. Model Size

- **Binary variables:** $|\mathcal{T}||\mathcal{S}|(1 + |\mathcal{K}|) + |\mathcal{P}||\mathcal{S}|$
- **Continuous variables:** $6|\mathcal{T}||\mathcal{S}| + |\mathcal{T}|$
- **Constraints:** dominated by (C10)–(C11) and (C13), scaling with $|\mathcal{P}||\mathcal{S}|$ and $|\mathcal{T}||\mathcal{S}||\mathcal{K}|^2$ respectively.

This is a self-contained **mixed-integer linear program** solvable by standard branch-and-bound / branch-and-cut solvers (Gurobi, CPLEX, SCIP) for realistic instance sizes.

Text:
# A Complete MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

## 1. Problem Setting and Assumptions

We consider a single high-speed railway line with a set of stations and segments, where a **partial segment blockage** occurs: one track direction of a segment is unavailable during a disruption time window. Trains may **reroute** onto the opposite track within the disruption window, requiring bidirectional conflict resolution. We integrate **train rescheduling (TRP)** and **train speed management (TSMP)** into one MILP.

**Assumptions (marked as such where not explicitly given in the input):**

- **(A1)** The line is discretized into a set of segments $e \in E$ between consecutive stations; each segment has a physical length $L_e$ and a free-flow running time $T_e^{\min}$.
- **(A2)** Each segment has two directional tracks (up/down). During the disruption window $[t^{\text{dis}}_e, \bar{t}^{\text{dis}}_e]$ on segment $e$, one track is blocked; trains may use the opposite track (rerouting) subject to headway and safety constraints.
- **(A3)** Train speed profiles are approximated by a finite set of **speed levels** $v \in V$ (e.g., discrete throttle/brake settings), each associated with an acceleration $a_v$ and energy rate $p_v$ (per unit time). This is a standard linearization for MILP tractability.
- **(A4)** Dwell times at stations are decision variables bounded by $[\underline{d}_i, \bar{d}_i]$ for train $i$.
- **(A5)** Minimum headway $h^{\min}$ between consecutive trains on the same track (same direction) and $h^{\text{bi}}$ for bidirectional (opposite direction) usage of the same track.
- **(A6)** Trains cannot overtake within a segment (no in-segment overtaking); reordering is only allowed at stations.
- **(A7)** Cancellation is allowed at a penalty cost $C^{\text{cancel}}_i$.
- **(A8)** The planning horizon is discretized into time steps $\Delta t$; all times are integer multiples of $\Delta t$.

---

## 2. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|---|---|
| $I$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations, indexed by $s$ |
| $E$ | Set of segments, indexed by $e$; segment $e$ connects station $s_e$ and $s_e+1$ |
| $V$ | Set of speed levels, indexed by $v$ |
| $D$ | Set of directions, $D=\{\text{up}, \text{down}\}$ |
| $T$ | Set of discrete time steps, indexed by $t$ |
| $E^{\text{dis}} \subseteq E$ | Segments affected by the partial blockage |
| $I^{\text{aff}} \subseteq I$ | Trains affected by the disruption |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Rescheduling (TRP) variables

- $x_{i,s} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ is **cancelled** at or before station $s$ (0 otherwise).
- $a_{i,s} \ge 0$: arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$.
- $d_{i,s} \ge 0$: departure time of train $i$ from station $s$.
- $w_{i,s} \ge 0$: dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$, $w_{i,s} = d_{i,s} - a_{i,s}$.
- $y_{i,j,s} \in \{0,1\}$: **ordering** variable — 1 if train $i$ departs station $s$ before train $j$ (for $i \neq j$, same direction).
- $r_{i,e} \in \{0,1\}$: **rerouting** variable — 1 if train $i$ uses the opposite track on segment $e$ (only relevant if $e \in E^{\text{dis}}$).
- $\delta_{i,e} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $e$ during the disruption window (used to enforce rerouting).

### 3.2 Speed management (TSMP) variables

- $u_{i,e,v} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if train $i$ uses speed level $v$ on segment $e$.
- $t^{\text{run}}_{i,e} \ge 0$: running time of train $i$ on segment $e$.
- $E^{\text{energy}}_{i,e} \ge 0$: energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $e$.

### 3.3 Auxiliary variables

- $z_{i,j,e} \in \{0,1\}$: 1 if trains $i$ and $j$ (opposite directions) both use the same track on segment $e$ (conflict indicator).
- $\sigma_{i,j,e} \in \{0,1\}$: sequencing variable for bidirectional conflict on segment $e$.

---

## 4. Objective Function

Minimize a weighted sum of total delay, energy consumption, and cancellations:

$$
\min \; Z = \alpha \sum_{i \in I} \sum_{s \in S} \big( a_{i,s} - a^{\text{sch}}_{i,s} \big)^+ 
+ \beta \sum_{i \in I} \sum_{e \in E} E^{\text{energy}}_{i,e}
+ \gamma \sum_{i \in I} \sum_{s \in S} C^{\text{cancel}}_i \, x_{i,s}
+ \lambda \sum_{i \in I} \sum_{e \in E} t^{\text{run}}_{i,e}
$$

where $(\cdot)^+ = \max(0, \cdot)$ is linearized via auxiliary variables $a^{\text{delay}}_{i,s} \ge a_{i,s} - a^{\text{sch}}_{i,s}$, $a^{\text{delay}}_{i,s} \ge 0$. Weights $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \lambda \ge 0$ balance the objectives.

**Linearized objective:**

$$
\min \; Z = \alpha \sum_{i,s} a^{\text{delay}}_{i,s} + \beta \sum_{i,e} E^{\text{energy}}_{i,e} + \gamma \sum_{i,s} C^{\text{cancel}}_i x_{i,s} + \lambda \sum_{i,e} t^{\text{run}}_{i,e}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Timetable and running-time consistency

**(C1) Arrival–departure–running linkage:**

$$
a_{i,s+1} = d_{i,s} + t^{\text{run}}_{i,e(s)}, \quad \forall i \in I,\; e(s) \in E
$$

**(C2) Dwell time bounds:**

$$
\underline{d}_i \le w_{i,s} = d_{i,s} - a_{i,s} \le \bar{d}_i, \quad \forall i, s
$$

**(C3) Departure after arrival:**

$$
d_{i,s} \ge a_{i,s}, \quad \forall i, s
$$

**(C4) Scheduled departure time (if not cancelled):**

$$
d_{i,s} \ge d^{\text{sch}}_{i,s} - M(1 - x_{i,s}), \quad \forall i, s
$$

**(C5) Cancellation propagation:**

$$
x_{i,s} \le x_{i,s+1}, \quad \forall i, s
$$

### 5.2 Speed profile selection

**(C6) One speed level per segment:**

$$
\sum_{v \in V} u_{i,e,v} = 1, \quad \forall i, e
$$

**(C7) Running time as a function of speed level:**

$$
t^{\text{run}}_{i,e} = \sum_{v \in V} \tau_{e,v} \, u_{i,e,v}, \quad \forall i, e
$$

where $\tau_{e,v} = L_e / v$ is the nominal running time at speed level $v$.

**(C8) Energy consumption as a function of speed level:**

$$
E^{\text{energy}}_{i,e} = \sum_{v \in V} p_v \, \tau_{e,v} \, u_{i,e,v}, \quad \forall i, e
$$

**(C9) Minimum running time (physical feasibility):**

$$
t^{\text{run}}_{i,e} \ge T_e^{\min}, \quad \forall i, e
$$

### 5.3 Headway and ordering constraints (same direction)

**(C10) Ordering consistency:**

$$
y_{i,j,s} + y_{j,i,s} = 1, \quad \forall i \neq j \in I,\; s \in S
$$

**(C11) Headway on departure (same direction):**

$$
d_{j,s} \ge d_{i,s} + h^{\min} - M(1 - y_{i,j,s}), \quad \forall i \neq j,\; s
$$

**(C12) Headway on arrival (same direction):**

$$
a_{j,s} \ge a_{i,s} + h^{\min} - M(1 - y_{i,j,s}), \quad \forall i \neq j,\; s
$$

**(C13) No overtaking within a segment (order preserved):**

$$
y_{i,j,s} = y_{i,j,s+1}, \quad \forall i \neq j,\; s, s+1
$$

### 5.4 Rerouting and disruption constraints

**(C14) Rerouting only on disrupted segments:**

$$
r_{i,e} = 0, \quad \forall i, e \notin E^{\text{dis}}
$$

**(C15) Disruption window detection:**

$$
\delta_{i,e} \ge 1 - M\big( (t^{\text{dis}}_e - d_{i,s_e})^+ + (a_{i,s_e+1} - \bar{t}^{\text{dis}}_e)^+ \big), \quad \forall i, e \in E^{\text{dis}}
$$

*(Linearized: $\delta_{i,e} = 1$ if train $i$'s traversal of $e$ overlaps $[t^{\text{dis}}_e, \bar{t}^{\text{dis}}_e]$.)*

**(C16) Mandatory rerouting during disruption:**

$$
r_{i,e} \ge \delta_{i,e}, \quad \forall i, e \in E^{\text{dis}}
$$

**(C17) Rerouting capacity (only one train per direction on opposite track):**

$$
\sum_{i \in I^{\text{aff}}} r_{i,e} \le 1, \quad \forall e \in E^{\text{dis}},\; \text{per direction}
$$

### 5.5 Bidirectional conflict resolution

**(C18) Conflict indicator:**

$$
z_{i,j,e} \ge r_{i,e} + r_{j,e} - 1, \quad \forall i \neq j,\; e \in E^{\text{dis}}
$$

**(C19) Bidirectional headway (if both use same track):**

$$
a_{j,s_e+1} \ge a_{i,s_e+1} + h^{\text{bi}} - M(1 - \sigma_{i,j,e}) - M(1 - z_{i,j,e}), \quad \forall i \neq j,\; e
$$

$$
a_{i,s_e+1} \ge a_{j,s_e+1} + h^{\text{bi}} - M \sigma_{i,j,e} - M(1 - z_{i,j,e}), \quad \forall i \neq j,\; e
$$

**(C20) Sequencing exclusivity:**

$$
\sigma_{i,j,e} + \sigma_{j,i,e} = 1, \quad \forall i \neq j,\; e \in E^{\text{dis}}
$$

### 5.6 Station capacity and resource constraints

**(C21) Platform capacity at station $s$:**

$$
\sum_{i \in I} \mathbb{1}[a_{i,s} \le t \le d_{i,s}] \le C^{\text{plat}}_s, \quad \forall s, t
$$

*(Linearized via occupancy variables $\phi_{i,s,t} \in \{0,1\}$ with big-M linking.)*

**(C22) Segment capacity (at most one train per direction per segment at a time):**

$$
\sum_{i \in I} \psi_{i,e,t} \le 1, \quad \forall e, t, \text{per direction}
$$

where $\psi_{i,e,t} = 1$ if train $i$ occupies segment $e$ at time $t$.

### 5.7 Variable domains

$$
a_{i,s}, d_{i,s}, w_{i,s}, t^{\text{run}}_{i,e}, E^{\text{energy}}_{i,e} \ge 0
$$

$$
x_{i,s}, y_{i,j,s}, r_{i,e}, \delta_{i,e}, u_{i,e,v}, z_{i,j,e}, \sigma_{i,j,e}, \phi_{i,s,t}, \psi_{i,e,t} \in \{0,1\}
$$

---

## 6. Model Summary

The complete MILP is:

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & Z = \alpha \sum_{i,s} a^{\text{delay}}_{i,s} + \beta \sum_{i,e} E^{\text{energy}}_{i,e} + \gamma \sum_{i,s} C^{\text{cancel}}_i x_{i,s} + \lambda \sum_{i,e} t^{\text{run}}_{i,e} \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & \text{(C1)–(C22)} \\
& \text{variable domains as specified}
\end{aligned}
}
$$

---

## 7. Key Modeling Features

1. **Integration of TRP and TSMP:** Constraints (C1)–(C5) handle rescheduling; (C6)–(C9) handle speed management; (C1) couples them via running times.
2. **Rerouting with bidirectional conflicts:** (C14)–(C20) model partial blockage rerouting and resolve bidirectional track-sharing conflicts.
3. **Conflict-free guarantee:** Headway constraints (C11)–(C12), (C19), and capacity constraints (C21)–(C22) ensure a conflict-free timetable.
4. **Energy efficiency:** Objective includes energy term $\beta \sum E^{\text{energy}}_{i,e}$, capturing the trade-off between delay and energy.
5. **Linear structure:** All constraints are linear (big-M reformulations for disjunctions), making the model solvable by standard MILP solvers (e.g., Gurobi, CPLEX).

---

## 8. Assumptions Recap (marked)

- **(A1)–(A8)** as stated in Section 1 are reasonable modeling assumptions not fully specified in the input.
- Speed levels $V$ and energy rates $p_v$ are assumed discretized; if continuous speed control is required, a piecewise-linear approximation can replace (C6)–(C8).
- The disruption window $[t^{\text{dis}}_e, \bar{t}^{\text{dis}}_e]$ is assumed known and fixed.
- Weights $\alpha, \beta, \gamma, \lambda$ are assumed given by the operator's policy.

Text:
# A Complete MILP Model for the Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) under Partial Segment Blockages

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $\mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j$ |
| $\mathcal{S}$ | Set of stations/segments along the line, indexed by $s$ |
| $\mathcal{B}$ | Set of block sections (track segments between consecutive stations), indexed by $b$ |
| $\mathcal{D} \subseteq \mathcal{B}$ | Set of disrupted block sections (partial segment blockages) |
| $\mathcal{K}$ | Set of speed levels (discrete speed profile segments), indexed by $k$ |
| $\mathcal{P}_i$ | Set of feasible speed profiles for train $i$ |
| $\mathcal{R}$ | Set of available routes (tracks) on each block, indexed by $r$; $\mathcal{R} = \{1, 2\}$ (up/down tracks) |
| $\mathcal{T}^{up} \subseteq \mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains traveling in the up direction |
| $\mathcal{T}^{down} \subseteq \mathcal{T}$ | Set of trains traveling in the down direction |

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T^{dep}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $T^{arr}_{i,s}$ | Scheduled arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $t^{min}_{i,b}$ | Minimum running time of train $i$ on block $b$ |
| $t^{max}_{i,b}$ | Maximum running time of train $i$ on block $b$ |
| $d^{min}_{i,s}$ | Minimum dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $d^{max}_{i,s}$ | Maximum dwell time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $h^{min}$ | Minimum headway (safety separation) between consecutive trains on the same track |
| $W_b$ | Disruption time window on block $b \in \mathcal{D}$: $[W_b^{start}, W_b^{end}]$ |
| $E_{i,k,b}$ | Energy consumption of train $i$ on block $b$ using speed level $k$ |
| $C^{delay}$ | Unit cost of delay (per time unit per train) |
| $C^{energy}$ | Unit cost of energy consumption |
| $C^{cancel}_i$ | Cost of canceling train $i$ |
| $C^{reroute}$ | Cost of rerouting a train to the opposite track |
| $M$ | A sufficiently large constant (big-M) |
| $v^{max}_k$ | Maximum speed associated with speed level $k$ |
| $a^{max}$ | Maximum acceleration |
| $a^{min}$ | Maximum deceleration (braking) |
| $\ell_b$ | Length of block section $b$ |

## 3. Decision Variables

### 3.1 Train Rescheduling Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $x_{i,s}$ | Continuous | Actual departure time of train $i$ from station $s$ |
| $y_{i,s}$ | Continuous | Actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $z_{i,b}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ is rerouted to the opposite track on block $b$; 0 otherwise |
| $u_{i,b}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ traverses block $b$; 0 if canceled on that block |
| $\delta_{i,j,b}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on block $b$ (sequencing variable) |
| $\gamma_{i,b}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ traverses block $b$ during the disruption window |
| $w_{i}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ is canceled entirely |

### 3.2 Speed Management Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $\lambda_{i,p}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ uses speed profile $p \in \mathcal{P}_i$; 0 otherwise |
| $v_{i,b,k}$ | Binary | 1 if train $i$ operates at speed level $k$ on block $b$ |
| $t^{run}_{i,b}$ | Continuous | Actual running time of train $i$ on block $b$ |
| $e_{i,b}$ | Continuous | Energy consumption of train $i$ on block $b$ |

### 3.3 Auxiliary Variables

| Variable | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| $\Delta^+_{i,s}$ | Continuous | Positive delay of train $i$ at station $s$ (actual − scheduled) |
| $\Delta^-_{i,s}$ | Continuous | Negative deviation (early arrival) of train $i$ at station $s$ |
| $\theta_{i,j,b}$ | Continuous | Time separation between trains $i$ and $j$ on block $b$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

The objective minimizes a weighted combination of total passenger delay, energy consumption, cancellation costs, and rerouting costs:

$$
\min \quad Z = \underbrace{C^{delay} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} \Delta^+_{i,s}}_{\text{Total delay cost}} 
+ \underbrace{C^{energy} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{b \in \mathcal{B}} e_{i,b}}_{\text{Total energy cost}} 
+ \underbrace{\sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} C^{cancel}_i \cdot w_i}_{\text{Cancellation cost}} 
+ \underbrace{C^{reroute} \sum_{i \in \mathcal{T}} \sum_{b \in \mathcal{D}} z_{i,b}}_{\text{Rerouting cost}}
\tag{1}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Timetable Constraints

#### 5.1.1 Arrival and Departure Time Relationships

For each train $i$ and station $s$ (except the origin and destination):

$$
y_{i,s} = x_{i,s-1} + t^{run}_{i,s-1} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \setminus \{s^{orig}_i\}
\tag{2}
$$

$$
x_{i,s} = y_{i,s} + d_{i,s} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S} \setminus \{s^{dest}_i\}
\tag{3}
$$

where $d_{i,s}$ is the actual dwell time at station $s$.

#### 5.1.2 Dwell Time Bounds

$$
d^{min}_{i,s} \cdot u_{i,s} \leq d_{i,s} \leq d^{max}_{i,s} \cdot u_{i,s} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
\tag{4}
$$

#### 5.1.3 Running Time Bounds

$$
t^{min}_{i,b} \cdot u_{i,b} \leq t^{run}_{i,b} \leq t^{max}_{i,b} \cdot u_{i,b} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; b \in \mathcal{B}
\tag{5}
$$

#### 5.1.4 Delay Definition

$$
\Delta^+_{i,s} - \Delta^-_{i,s} = y_{i,s} - T^{arr}_{i,s} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
\tag{6}
$$

$$
\Delta^+_{i,s} \geq 0, \quad \Delta^-_{i,s} \geq 0 \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; s \in \mathcal{S}
\tag{7}
$$

#### 5.1.5 Train Cancellation Logic

$$
u_{i,b} \leq 1 - w_i \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; b \in \mathcal{B}
\tag{8}
$$

$$
u_{i,b} \geq u_{i,b+1} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; b \in \mathcal{B} \setminus \{b^{last}\}
\tag{9}
$$

Constraint (9) ensures that if a train is canceled on a block, it is also canceled on all subsequent blocks (monotonicity of cancellation).

---

### 5.2 Disruption and Rerouting Constraints

#### 5.2.1 Disruption Window Constraint

A train cannot traverse a disrupted block $b \in \mathcal{D}$ during the disruption window $[W_b^{start}, W_b^{end}]$ unless it is rerouted:

$$
y_{i,b} \geq W_b^{end} - M(1 - \gamma_{i,b}) - M \cdot z_{i,b} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; b \in \mathcal{D}
\tag{10}
$$

$$
x_{i,b} \leq W_b^{start} + M \cdot \gamma_{i,b} + M \cdot z_{i,b} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; b \in \mathcal{D}
\tag{11}
$$

where $\gamma_{i,b} = 1$ indicates that train $i$ would like to traverse block $b$ during the disruption window (and thus must either wait or reroute).

#### 5.2.2 Rerouting Feasibility

Rerouting is only permitted on disrupted blocks:

$$
z_{i,b} = 0 \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; b \in \mathcal{B} \setminus \mathcal{D}
\tag{12}
$$

#### 5.2.3 Rerouting and Track Capacity

When train $i$ is rerouted on block $b$, it uses the opposite track. This creates potential conflicts with trains traveling in the opposite direction:

$$
z_{i,b} + z_{j,b} \leq 1 \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}^{up}, \; j \in \mathcal{T}^{down}, \; b \in \mathcal{D} \text{ if } i, j \text{ would conflict}
\tag{13}
$$

*(Assumption: At most one train can be rerouted to the opposite track at any given time on a block, ensuring unidirectional capacity is maintained.)*

---

### 5.3 Conflict-Free Constraints (Headway and Sequencing)

#### 5.3.1 Sequencing on Shared Tracks

For any two trains $i, j$ traversing the same block $b$ on the same track (including rerouted trains):

$$
y_{j,b} \geq x_{i,b} + h^{min} - M(1 - \delta_{i,j,b}) - M(1 - u_{i,b}) - M(1 - u_{j,b}) \quad \forall i \neq j, \; b \in \mathcal{B}
\tag{14}
$$

$$
y_{i,b} \geq x_{j,b} + h^{min} - M \cdot \delta_{i,j,b} - M(1 - u_{i,b}) - M(1 - u_{j,b}) \quad \forall i \neq j, \; b \in \mathcal{B}
\tag{15}
$$

$$
\delta_{i,j,b} + \delta_{j,i,b} = 1 \quad \forall i \neq j, \; b \in \mathcal{B} \text{ if both trains use block } b
\tag{16}
$$

#### 5.3.2 Bidirectional Conflict on Rerouted Segments

When train $i$ is rerouted to the opposite track on block $b$, it may conflict with trains $j$ traveling in the opposite direction on their normal track:

$$
y_{j,b} \geq x_{i,b} + h^{min} - M(1 - z_{i,b}) - M(1 - u_{j,b}) \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}^{up}, \; j \in \mathcal{T}^{down}, \; b \in \mathcal{D}
\tag{17}
$$

$$
y_{i,b} \geq x_{j,b} + h^{min} - M(1 - z_{i,b}) - M(1 - u_{j,b}) \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}^{up}, \; j \in \mathcal{T}^{down}, \; b \in \mathcal{D}
\tag{18}
$$

*(Assumption: Constraints (17)–(18) ensure that a rerouted train does not conflict with opposite-direction trains on the shared track.)*

---

### 5.4 Speed Profile and Energy Constraints

#### 5.4.1 Speed Profile Selection

Each train selects exactly one speed profile (if not canceled):

$$
\sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} \lambda_{i,p} = 1 - w_i \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}
\tag{19}
$$

#### 5.4.2 Linking Speed Profiles to Running Times

$$
t^{run}_{i,b} = \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} \tau_{i,b,p} \cdot \lambda_{i,p} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; b \in \mathcal{B}
\tag{20}
$$

where $\tau_{i,b,p}$ is the running time on block $b$ under speed profile $p$.

#### 5.4.3 Energy Consumption

$$
e_{i,b} = \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i} E_{i,b,p} \cdot \lambda_{i,p} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; b \in \mathcal{B}
\tag{21}
$$

#### 5.4.4 Speed Level Consistency

$$
v_{i,b,k} = \sum_{p \in \mathcal{P}_i : k \in p} \lambda_{i,p} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; b \in \mathcal{B}, \; k \in \mathcal{K}
\tag{22}
$$

#### 5.4.5 Acceleration and Deceleration Feasibility

The transition between speed levels on consecutive blocks must respect physical limits:

$$
\frac{v^{max}_{k'} - v^{max}_{k}}{\Delta t} \leq a^{max} \quad \text{if } v^{max}_{k'} > v^{max}_{k}
\tag{23}
$$

$$
\frac{v^{max}_{k} - v^{max}_{k'}}{\Delta t} \leq |a^{min}| \quad \text{if } v^{max}_{k} > v^{max}_{k'}
\tag{24}
$$

*(Assumption: These constraints are embedded in the generation of feasible speed profiles $\mathcal{P}_i$; they are not explicit decision constraints but rather pre-processing conditions.)*

---

### 5.5 Coupling Constraints between Rescheduling and Speed Management

#### 5.5.1 Running Time Consistency

The actual running time on each block must be consistent with the selected speed profile:

$$
t^{run}_{i,b} = y_{i,b} - x_{i,b-1} \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; b \in \mathcal{B}
\tag{25}
$$

#### 5.5.2 Arrival Time at Disrupted Block

For disrupted blocks, the arrival time must account for the disruption window:

$$
y_{i,b} \geq W_b^{end} \cdot (1 - z_{i,b}) \quad \forall i \in \mathcal{T}, \; b \in \mathcal{D}
\tag{26}
$$

*(Assumption: If a train is not rerouted, it must arrive at the disrupted block after the disruption window ends.)*

#### 5.5.3 Energy-Delay Trade-off

The model implicitly captures the trade-off: faster speed profiles reduce delay but increase energy consumption, as encoded in equations (20)–(21) and the objective function (1).

---

### 5.6 Domain Constraints

$$
x_{i,s}, \; y_{i,s}, \; t^{run}_{i,b}, \; e_{i,b}, \; \Delta^+_{i,s}, \; \Delta^-_{i,s}, \; \theta_{i,j,b} \geq 0
\tag{27}
$$

$$
z_{i,b}, \; u_{i,b}, \; \delta_{i,j,b}, \; \gamma_{i,b}, \; w_i, \; \lambda_{i,p}, \; v_{i,b,k} \in \{0, 1\}
\tag{28}
$$

---

## 6. Assumptions

1. **Discrete Speed Profiles**: Speed profiles are pre-computed and discretized into a finite set $\mathcal{P}_i$ for each train, each associated with a specific running time and energy consumption. *(Reasonable assumption for MILP tractability.)*

2. **Single-Track Rerouting**: Rerouting allows a train to use the opposite track on a disrupted block, but at most one train can be rerouted at a time on a given block to maintain unidirectional capacity. *(Assumption based on the problem description.)*

3. **No Overtaking on Blocks**: Trains cannot overtake each other within a block section; sequencing is determined at block entry. *(Standard assumption in railway scheduling.)*

4. **Deterministic Disruption Window**: The disruption window $[W_b^{start}, W_b^{end}]$ is known and fixed. *(Assumption for deterministic optimization.)*

5. **Fixed Station Infrastructure**: The number of tracks at stations is sufficient to accommodate dwell times without additional conflicts. *(Simplification assumption.)*

6. **Energy Consumption Linear in Speed Profile**: Energy consumption is pre-computed for each speed profile and does not depend on real-time decisions. *(Assumption for linearity.)*

7. **Cancellation Monotonicity**: If a train is canceled on a block, it is canceled on all subsequent blocks. *(Operational assumption.)*

8. **No Passenger Transfer Considerations**: The model focuses on train operations and does not explicitly model passenger transfers. *(Simplification assumption.)*

---

## 7. Model Summary

The proposed MILP integrates train rescheduling (retiming, reordering, rerouting, cancellation) with speed management (speed profile selection, energy consumption) under partial segment blockages. The objective (1) minimizes delay, energy, cancellation, and rerouting costs. Constraints (2)–(28) ensure:

- Timetable feasibility (2)–(9)
- Disruption handling and rerouting (10)–(13)
- Conflict-free operations (14)–(18)
- Speed profile and energy consistency (19)–(24)
- Coupling between rescheduling and speed management (25)–(26)
- Variable domains (27)–(28)

This formulation provides a complete, linear model for the TRSMP, capturing the interdependencies between traffic-level decisions and train dynamics while ensuring conflict-free operations on shared tracks.

Text:
# MILP Formulation: Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $I$ | Set of trains, indexed by $i, j \in I$ |
| $K$ | Set of stations/stops, indexed by $k = 1, \dots, K$ |
| $S$ | Set of segments, indexed by $s = 1, \dots, S$ (segment $s$ connects station $s$ and $s+1$) |
| $M$ | Set of discrete speed levels (running-time options), indexed by $m \in M$ |
| $D \subseteq S$ | Set of disrupted segments |
| $I^{up} \subseteq I$ | Set of trains running in the "up" (normal) direction |
| $I^{dn} \subseteq I$ | Set of trains running in the "down" (opposite) direction |

**Assumption A5 (extended):** Each train $i$ has a fixed direction; $I^{up} \cap I^{dn} = \emptyset$, $I^{up} \cup I^{dn} = I$.

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $L_s$ | Length of segment $s$ [km] |
| $V_s^{\max}$ | Maximum allowed speed on segment $s$ [km/h] |
| $a_{i,k}^{\text{plan}}$ | Planned arrival time of train $i$ at station $k$ |
| $d_{i,k}^{\text{plan}}$ | Planned departure time of train $i$ from station $k$ |
| $r_{i,s}^{\text{plan}}$ | Planned running time of train $i$ on segment $s$ |
| $h_{\min}$ | Minimum headway (same track, same direction) |
| $h_{\text{opp}}$ | Minimum separation (same track, opposite directions) |
| $dw_{\min}, dw_{\max}$ | Min/max dwell time at a station |
| $e_{i,s,m}$ | Energy consumption of train $i$ on segment $s$ at speed level $m$ |
| $rt_{i,s,m}$ | Running time of train $i$ on segment $s$ at speed level $m$ |
| $v_{s,m}$ | Speed value associated with level $m$ on segment $s$ |
| $\Delta v_{\max}$ | Max allowed speed change between adjacent segments |
| $c_{\text{delay}}$ | Penalty per unit of delay (per train per station) |
| $c_{\text{cancel}}$ | Penalty for cancelling a train |
| $c_{\text{energy}}$ | Weight on energy consumption |
| $T_{\text{start}}, T_{\text{end}}$ | Disruption time window |
| $T_{\max}$ | End of planning horizon |
| $M^{big}$ | Sufficiently large constant |

**Assumption A4:** Speed profiles are discretized into $|M|$ levels; $rt_{i,s,m} = L_s / v_{s,m}$ (piecewise-constant approximation).

**Assumption A8:** Energy is linear in speed level: $e_{i,s,m} = \alpha_i \cdot v_{s,m} \cdot L_s$ (or given tabulated values).

---

## 3. Decision Variables

### Continuous variables
| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $a_{i,k}$ | $\geq 0$ | Actual arrival time of train $i$ at station $k$ |
| $d_{i,k}$ | $\geq 0$ | Actual departure time of train $i$ from station $k$ |
| $\delta_{i,k}$ | $\geq 0$ | Delay of train $i$ at station $k$ |

### Binary variables
| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| $x_{i,s,m}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $s$ at speed level $m$ |
| $y_{i,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses the opposite track on segment $s$ |
| $z_i$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ is cancelled |
| $o_{i,j,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ precedes train $j$ on segment $s$ (same direction, same track) |
| $p_{i,j,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ uses segment $s$ before train $j$ (opposite directions, shared track) |
| $u_{i,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if train $i$ traverses segment $s$ during the disruption window |
| $\sigma_{i,j,s}$ | $\{0,1\}$ | 1 if trains $i$ and $j$ use different tracks on segment $s$ |

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min \; Z = c_{\text{delay}} \sum_{i \in I} \sum_{k \in K} \delta_{i,k}
\;+\; c_{\text{cancel}} \sum_{i \in I} z_i
\;+\; c_{\text{energy}} \sum_{i \in I} \sum_{s \in S} \sum_{m \in M} e_{i,s,m} \, x_{i,s,m}
$$

**Interpretation:**
- First term: total weighted delay across all trains and stations.
- Second term: penalty for cancelled services.
- Third term: total energy consumption weighted by $c_{\text{energy}}$.

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Speed Level Selection

For each train $i \in I$ and segment $s \in S$:

$$
\sum_{m \in M} x_{i,s,m} = 1 - z_i \tag{C1}
$$

**Explanation:** A non-cancelled train must select exactly one speed level per segment; a cancelled train selects none.

---

### 5.2 Running Time Definition

For each train $i \in I$ and segment $s \in S$ (segment $s$ connects station $s$ and $s+1$):

$$
a_{i,s+1} = d_{i,s} + \sum_{m \in M} rt_{i,s,m} \, x_{i,s,m} \tag{C2}
$$

**Explanation:** Arrival at the next station equals departure from the current station plus the running time determined by the chosen speed level.

**Assumption A9:** Acceleration/deceleration is absorbed into the discrete running-time options; no separate dynamics constraint is needed beyond C10.

---

### 5.3 Dwell Time Constraints

For each train $i \in I$ and station $k \in K$:

$$
dw_{\min} (1 - z_i) \;\leq\; d_{i,k} - a_{i,k} \;\leq\; dw_{\max} (1 - z_i) \tag{C3}
$$

**Explanation:** Dwell time must lie within $[dw_{\min}, dw_{\max}]$ for active trains; for cancelled trains, $d_{i,k} = a_{i,k}$ (enforced by C5).

---

### 5.4 Delay Definition

For each train $i \in I$ and station $k \in K$:

$$
\delta_{i,k} \;\geq\; a_{i,k} - a_{i,k}^{\text{plan}} \tag{C4a}
$$
$$
\delta_{i,k} \;\geq\; 0 \tag{C4b}
$$

**Explanation:** Delay is the non-negative deviation from the planned arrival time.

---

### 5.5 Cancellation Constraints

For each train $i \in I$ and station $k \in K$:

$$
a_{i,k} \;\leq\; M^{big} (1 - z_i) \tag{C5a}
$$
$$
d_{i,k} \;\leq\; M^{big} (1 - z_i) \tag{C5b}
$$
$$
a_{i,k} \;\geq\; -M^{big} (1 - z_i) \tag{C5c}
$$
$$
d_{i,k} \;\geq\; -M^{big} (1 - z_i) \tag{C5d}
$$

**Explanation:** If $z_i = 1$, all times are forced to zero (or effectively removed from the model). If $z_i = 0$, the constraints are non-binding.

**Assumption A11:** Cancelled trains contribute zero delay and zero energy; their planned times are not counted.

---

### 5.6 Disruption / Rerouting Constraints

For each train $i \in I$ and disrupted segment $s \in D$:

**Step 1 — Detect traversal during disruption window:**

$$
a_{i,s} \;\leq\; T_{\text{end}} + M^{big}(1 - u_{i,s}) \tag{C6a}
$$
$$
a_{i,s} \;\geq\; T_{\text{start}} - M^{big}(1 - u_{i,s}) \tag{C6b}
$$
$$
a_{i,s} \;\leq\; T_{\text{start}} - \epsilon + M^{big} \, u_{i,s} \tag{C6c}
$$
$$
a_{i,s} \;\geq\; T_{\text{end}} + \epsilon - M^{big} \, u_{i,s} \tag{C6d}
$$

**Explanation:** $u_{i,s} = 1$ iff train $i$ enters segment $s$ within $[T_{\text{start}}, T_{\text{end}}]$. Constraints (C6a)–(C6b) force $u_{i,s} = 1$ if $a_{i,s} \in [T_{\text{start}}, T_{\text{end}}]$; (C6c)–(C6d) force $u_{i,s} = 0$ otherwise.

**Step 2 — Force rerouting on blocked segments:**

$$
y_{i,s} \;\geq\; u_{i,s} \tag{C6e}
$$

**Explanation:** If a train traverses a disrupted segment during the window, it must use the opposite track ($y_{i,s} = 1$).

**Assumption A3:** The normal track is completely unavailable on $s \in D$ during $[T_{\text{start}}, T_{\text{end}}]$.

---

### 5.7 Same-Direction Headway (Same Track)

For each segment $s \in S$ and each pair of trains $i, j \in I$ with the same direction:

**Track-difference linearization:**

$$
\sigma_{i,j,s} \;\geq\; y_{i,s} - y_{j,s} \tag{C7a}
$$
$$
\sigma_{i,j,s} \;\geq\; y_{j,s} - y_{i,s} \tag{C7b}
$$

**Ordering constraints:**

$$
a_{j,s} \;\geq\; a_{i,s} + h_{\min} - M^{big}(1 - o_{i,j,s}) - M^{big} \, \sigma_{i,j,s} \tag{C7c}
$$

$$
o_{i,j,s} + o_{j,i,s} = 1 \quad (i \neq j) \tag{C7d}
$$

**Explanation:** If trains $i$ and $j$ use the same track ($\sigma_{i,j,s} = 0$) and $i$ precedes $j$ ($o_{i,j,s} = 1$), then $j$ must enter segment $s$ at least $h_{\min}$ after $i$. If they use different tracks, the constraint is relaxed.

**Assumption A6:** Headway applies at segment entry; a more detailed model could enforce it at multiple points.

---

### 5.8 Opposite-Direction Conflict on Shared Track

For each segment $s \in S$ and each pair $(i, j)$ with $i \in I^{up}$, $j \in I^{dn}$:

$$
a_{j,s} \;\geq\; a_{i,s} + h_{\text{opp}} - M^{big}(1 - p_{i,j,s}) - M^{big} \, \sigma_{i,j,s} \tag{C8a}
$$

$$
a_{i,s} \;\geq\; a_{j,s} + h_{\text{opp}} - M^{big} \, p_{i,j,s} - M^{big} \, \sigma_{i,j,s} \tag{C8b}
$$

$$
p_{i,j,s} + p_{j,i,s} = 1 \quad \text{(if same track)} \tag{C8c}
$$

**Explanation:** If two opposite-direction trains share a track ($\sigma_{i,j,s} = 0$), one must clear the segment before the other enters, with separation $h_{\text{opp}}$. If they use different tracks, constraints are relaxed.

**Assumption A6 (extended):** $h_{\text{opp}}$ accounts for the time needed for the first train to fully clear the segment (meet time).

---

### 5.9 Rerouting Capacity

For each segment $s \in S$ and each track $q \in \{0, 1\}$:

At most one train can occupy a track at a time — this is implied by C7 and C8 (headway constraints ensure temporal separation). No additional constraint is needed.

**Assumption A10:** The headway constraints (C7)–(C8) are sufficient to prevent simultaneous track occupancy.

---

### 5.10 Speed Continuity / Dynamics

For each train $i \in I$ and adjacent segments $s, s+1 \in S$:

$$
\left| \sum_{m \in M} v_{s,m} \, x_{i,s,m} - \sum_{m' \in M} v_{s+1,m'} \, x_{i,s+1,m'} \right| \;\leq\; \Delta v_{\max} \tag{C10}
$$

**Linearization:** Introduce auxiliary variables $\phi_{i,s}^+ \geq 0$, $\phi_{i,s}^- \geq 0$:

$$
\sum_{m} v_{s,m} x_{i,s,m} - \sum_{m'} v_{s+1,m'} x_{i,s+1,m'} = \phi_{i,s}^+ - \phi_{i,s}^- \tag{C10a}
$$
$$
\phi_{i,s}^+ + \phi_{i,s}^- \;\leq\; \Delta v_{\max} \tag{C10b}
$$

**Explanation:** The speed change between consecutive segments cannot exceed $\Delta v_{\max}$, approximating acceleration/deceleration feasibility.

**Assumption A9:** This is a simplified dynamics constraint; a full model would track acceleration explicitly.

---

### 5.11 Time Horizon and Non-Negativity

For each train $i \in I$ and station $k \in K$:

$$
0 \;\leq\; a_{i,k} \;\leq\; T_{\max} \tag{C11a}
$$
$$
0 \;\leq\; d_{i,k} \;\leq\; T_{\max} \tag{C11b}
$$

---

### 5.12 Binary and Integer Domains

$$
x_{i,s,m} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall i, s, m \tag{C12a}
$$
$$
y_{i,s} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall i, s \tag{C12b}
$$
$$
z_i \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall i \tag{C12c}
$$
$$
o_{i,j,s} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall i \neq j, s \tag{C12d}
$$
$$
p_{i,j,s} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall i \neq j, s \tag{C12e}
$$
$$
u_{i,s} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall i, s \in D \tag{C12f}
$$
$$
\sigma_{i,j,s} \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall i \neq j, s \tag{C12g}
$$

---

## 6. Complete MILP Summary

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & c_{\text{delay}} \sum_{i,k} \delta_{i,k} + c_{\text{cancel}} \sum_i z_i + c_{\text{energy}} \sum_{i,s,m} e_{i,s,m} x_{i,s,m} \\
\text{s.t.} \quad
& \sum_m x_{i,s,m} = 1 - z_i && \forall i, s \\
& a_{i,s+1} = d_{i,s} + \sum_m rt_{i,s,m} x_{i,s,m} && \forall i, s \\
& dw_{\min}(1-z_i) \leq d_{i,k} - a_{i,k} \leq dw_{\max}(1-z_i) && \forall i, k \\
& \delta_{i,k} \geq a_{i,k} - a_{i,k}^{\text{plan}}, \quad \delta_{i,k} \geq 0 && \forall i, k \\
& a_{i,k}, d_{i,k} \leq M^{big}(1-z_i), \quad a_{i,k}, d_{i,k} \geq -M^{big}(1-z_i) && \forall i, k \\
& \text{(C6a)--(C6e): disruption detection and rerouting} && \forall i, s \in D \\
& \text{(C7a)--(C7d): same-direction headway} && \forall i \neq j, s \\
& \text{(C8a)--(C8c): opposite-direction separation} && \forall i \in I^{up}, j \in I^{dn}, s \\
& \text{(C10a)--(C10b): speed continuity} && \forall i, s, s+1 \\
& 0 \leq a_{i,k}, d_{i,k} \leq T_{\max} && \forall i, k \\
& x, y, z, o, p, u, \sigma \in \{0,1\} &&
\end{aligned}
}
$$

---

## 7. Assumptions (Explicitly Marked)

| ID | Assumption |
|----|------------|
| **A1** | Line discretized into segments $s = 1..S$; each has length $L_s$ and max speed $V_s^{\max}$. |
| **A2** | Two tracks per segment: track 0 (normal direction) and track 1 (opposite). Rerouting = using track 1. |
| **A3** | Disruption blocks normal track on $D \subseteq S$ during $[T_{\text{start}}, T_{\text{end}}]$; trains must reroute or wait. |
| **A4** | Speed profiles discretized into $|M|$ levels; running time $rt_{i,s,m} = L_s / v_{s,m}$. |
| **A5** | Each train has a fixed direction ($I^{up}$ or $I^{dn}$); cancellation allowed with penalty. |
| **A6** | Minimum headway $h_{\min}$ (same direction) and $h_{\text{opp}}$ (opposite directions) apply at segment entry. |
| **A7** | Dwell times bounded by $[dw_{\min}, dw_{\max}]$; running times depend on speed level. |
| **A8** | Energy linear in speed level: $e_{i,s,m} = \alpha_i v_{s,m} L_s$ (or tabulated). |
| **A9** | Acceleration/deceleration approximated by speed-change limit $\Delta v_{\max}$ between adjacent segments. |
| **A10** | Headway constraints (C7)–(C8) are sufficient to prevent simultaneous track occupancy. |
| **A11** | Cancelled trains contribute zero delay and zero energy; their times are set to zero via BigM. |
| **A12** | The disruption window is fixed and known in advance (deterministic). |

---

## 8. Model Size and Complexity

| Component | Count |
|-----------|-------|
| Continuous variables | $2|I||K| + |I||K|$ (times + delays) |
| Binary variables | $|I||S||M| + |I||S| + |I| + 2|I|^2|S| + |I||D|$ |
| Constraints | $O(|I||S||M| + |I||S| + |I||K| + |I|^2|S|)$ |

**Complexity:** The model is a large-scale MILP. The quadratic terms in $|I|^2|S|$ (ordering variables) dominate. For realistic instances (e.g., 20 trains, 10 segments, 5 speed levels), the model has ~10,000 binaries and ~5,000 constraints — solvable with commercial solvers (Gurobi, CPLEX) using branch-and-bound with warm starts.

---

## 9. Key Modeling Choices and Justifications

1. **Discrete speed levels (A4):** Keeps the model linear; continuous speed control would introduce nonlinear running-time functions.
2. **BigM linearization (C5, C6, C7, C8):** Standard technique for disjunctive constraints; $M^{big}$ should be set to $T_{\max}$ or a tight upper bound.
3. **Ordering variables $o_{i,j,s}$ and $p_{i,j,s}$:** Encode the sequence of trains on each segment, enabling headway enforcement without time-indexed variables.
4. **Track indicator $\sigma_{i,j,s}$:** Linearizes the "same track" condition, allowing headway constraints to be relaxed when trains use different tracks.
5. **Speed continuity (C10):** A simplified proxy for acceleration/deceleration feasibility; more detailed dynamics would require additional state variables (velocity, position) and nonlinear constraints.

# Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP)
## Complete Mixed-Integer Linear Program — Best Model

---

## 1. Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $T$ | Set of trains, indexed by $t, t'$ |
| $S$ | Set of stations along the line, indexed by $s$ (ordered $1,\dots,|S|$) |
| $E$ | Set of segments between consecutive stations, $e=(s,s+1)$ |
| $E^{dis}\subseteq E$ | Segments inside the disruption area |
| $K$ | Set of discretized speed levels, indexed by $k$ |
| $T^{up}\subseteq T$ | Trains running in the up direction |
| $T^{dn}\subseteq T$ | Trains running in the down direction |
| $T^{aff}\subseteq T$ | Trains whose route passes through the disruption area |

---

## 2. Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| $L_e$ | Length of segment $e$ [km] |
| $v^{\max}_e$ | Speed limit on segment $e$ [km/h] |
| $v_k$ | Speed level $k$ [km/h] (increasing) |
| $a^{\max}, b^{\max}$ | Max acceleration / deceleration [km/h²] |
| $\Delta t$ | Time step for speed-profile transitions |
| $h$ | Minimum safety headway [min] |
| $\tau^{dwell,\min}_{t,s},\ \tau^{dwell,\max}_{t,s}$ | Min/max dwell time of train $t$ at station $s$ |
| $a^{nom}_{t,s},\ d^{nom}_{t,s}$ | Nominal arrival / departure times |
| $t_{start}, t_{end}$ | Disruption time window |
| $M$ | Large constant (big-M) |
| $w^{delay}, w^{cancel}, w^{energy}$ | Objective weights |
| $\alpha_k, \beta_k$ | Piecewise-linear energy coefficients for speed level $k$ |
| $C^{\max}$ | Maximum number of cancellations |

---

## 3. Decision Variables

**Scheduling**
- $a_{t,s}\ge 0$ — arrival time of train $t$ at station $s$ [min]
- $d_{t,s}\ge 0$ — departure time of train $t$ from station $s$ [min]
- $w_{t,s}\ge 0$ — dwell time of train $t$ at station $s$ [min]
- $\delta_{t,s}\ge 0$ — delay of train $t$ at station $s$ [min]

**Ordering / safety**
- $y_{t,t',s}\in\{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $t$ precedes train $t'$ at station/segment $s$

**Rerouting**
- $r_{t,e}\in\{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $t$ uses the opposite track on segment $e$ during disruption

**Speed profile**
- $u_{t,e,k}\in\{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $t$ uses speed level $k$ on segment $e$
- $v_{t,e}\ge 0$ — average speed of train $t$ on segment $e$ [km/h]
- $E_{t,e}\ge 0$ — energy consumed by train $t$ on segment $e$ [kWh]

**Cancellation**
- $c_t\in\{0,1\}$ — 1 if train $t$ is cancelled

---

## 4. Objective Function

$$
\min\; Z = w^{delay}\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{s\in S}\delta_{t,s}
\;+\; w^{cancel}\sum_{t\in T}c_t
\;+\; w^{energy}\sum_{t\in T}\sum_{e\in E}E_{t,e}
$$

---

## 5. Constraints

### 5.1 Timetable / Dwell

$$
d_{t,s} \ge a_{t,s} + \tau^{dwell,\min}_{t,s} - M\,c_t \qquad \forall t,s \tag{1}
$$
$$
d_{t,s} \le a_{t,s} + \tau^{dwell,\max}_{t,s} + M\,c_t \qquad \forall t,s \tag{2}
$$
$$
w_{t,s} = d_{t,s} - a_{t,s} \qquad \forall t,s \tag{3}
$$

### 5.2 Running Time Coupling (Speed ↔ Timetable)

$$
a_{t,s+1} - d_{t,s} \ge \sum_{k\in K}\frac{60\,L_e}{v_k}\,u_{t,e,k} - M\,c_t \qquad \forall t,\ e=(s,s+1) \tag{4}
$$

### 5.3 Delay Definition

$$
\delta_{t,s} \ge a_{t,s} - a^{nom}_{t,s} - M\,c_t \qquad \forall t,s \tag{5}
$$
$$
\delta_{t,s} \ge d_{t,s} - d^{nom}_{t,s} - M\,c_t \qquad \forall t,s \tag{6}
$$

### 5.4 Headway / Safety (same direction, same track)

For $t,t'$ in the same direction sharing segment $e=(s,s+1)$:

$$
d_{t',s} \ge d_{t,s} + h - M(1-y_{t,t',s}) - M(c_t+c_{t'}) \tag{7}
$$
$$
d_{t,s} \ge d_{t',s} + h - M\,y_{t,t',s} - M(c_t+c_{t'}) \tag{8}
$$
$$
y_{t,t',s} + y_{t',t,s} = 1 \qquad \forall t\ne t',\ s \tag{9}
$$

### 5.5 Disruption Constraints

**Rerouting only for affected trains, only on disruption segments, only if not cancelled:**
$$
r_{t,e} = 0 \qquad \forall t\notin T^{aff},\ e\notin E^{dis} \tag{10}
$$
$$
r_{t,e} \le 1 - c_t \qquad \forall t\in T^{aff},\ e\in E^{dis} \tag{11}
$$

**Rerouting only if train actually traverses the segment inside the disruption window:**
$$
d_{t,s} \le t_{end} + M(1-r_{t,e}) \qquad \forall t\in T^{aff},\ e=(s,s+1)\in E^{dis} \tag{12}
$$
$$
a_{t,s+1} \ge t_{start} - M(1-r_{t,e}) \qquad \forall t\in T^{aff},\ e=(s,s+1)\in E^{dis} \tag{13}
$$

**Blocked track — if not rerouted, train must clear segment before $t_{start}$ or enter after $t_{end}$:**
$$
d_{t,s} \le t_{start} + M(1-r_{t,e}) + M\,c_t \qquad \forall t\in T^{aff},\ e\in E^{dis} \tag{14}
$$
$$
a_{t,s+1} \ge t_{end} - M(1-r_{t,e}) - M\,c_t \qquad \forall t\in T^{aff},\ e\in E^{dis} \tag{15}
$$

### 5.6 Conflict-Free Shared Track (Bidirectional Rerouting)

For $t\in T^{up},\ t'\in T^{dn},\ e=(s,s+1)\in E^{dis}$:

$$
d_{t',s} \ge a_{t,s+1} + h - M(1-y_{t,t',e}) - M(2-r_{t,e}-r_{t',e}) \tag{16}
$$
$$
d_{t,s} \ge a_{t',s+1} + h - M\,y_{t,t',e} - M(2-r_{t,e}-r_{t',e}) \tag{17}
$$

### 5.7 Speed Profile

$$
\sum_{k\in K} u_{t,e,k} = 1 - c_t \qquad \forall t,e \tag{18}
$$
$$
v_{t,e} = \sum_{k\in K} v_k\,u_{t,e,k} \qquad \forall t,e \tag{19}
$$
$$
v_{t,e} \le v^{\max}_e + M\,c_t \qquad \forall t,e \tag{20}
$$
$$
u_{t,e,k} = 0 \quad \text{if } v_k > v^{\max}_e \tag{21}
$$

**Acceleration / deceleration limits between consecutive segments:**
$$
v_{t,e'} - v_{t,e} \le a^{\max}\Delta t + M\,c_t \qquad \forall t,\ e,e'\ \text{consecutive} \tag{22}
$$
$$
v_{t,e} - v_{t,e'} \le b^{\max}\Delta t + M\,c_t \qquad \forall t,\ e,e'\ \text{consecutive} \tag{23}
$$

### 5.8 Energy Consumption (Piecewise-Linear Lower Envelope)

$$
E_{t,e} \ge \alpha_k\,v_{t,e} + \beta_k - M(1-u_{t,e,k}) - M\,c_t \qquad \forall t,e,k \tag{24}
$$
$$
E_{t,e} \ge 0 \qquad \forall t,e \tag{25}
$$

### 5.9 Cancellation Logic

$$
a_{t,s} \le a^{nom}_{t,s} + M\,c_t,\quad a_{t,s} \ge a^{nom}_{t,s} - M\,c_t \qquad \forall t,s \tag{26}
$$
$$
d_{t,s} \le d^{nom}_{t,s} + M\,c_t,\quad d_{t,s} \ge d^{nom}_{t,s} - M\,c_t \qquad \forall t,s \tag{27}
$$
$$
c_t = 0 \qquad \forall t\notin T^{aff} \tag{28}
$$
$$
\sum_{t\in T} c_t \le C^{\max} \tag{29}
$$

### 5.10 Variable Domains

$$
a_{t,s},d_{t,s},w_{t,s},\delta_{t,s},v_{t,e},E_{t,e}\ge 0 \tag{30}
$$
$$
y_{t,t',s},\ r_{t,e},\ u_{t,e,k},\ c_t \in \{0,1\} \tag{31}
$$

---

## 6. Model Summary

| Component | Type | Count |
|-----------|------|-------|
| Continuous variables | $a,d,w,\delta,v,E$ | $O(|T||S| + |T||E|)$ |
| Binary variables | $y,r,u,c$ | $O(|T|^2|S| + |T||E||K|)$ |
| Constraints | (1)–(31) | $O(|T|^2|S| + |T||E||K|)$ |

**Model class:** MILP — linear objective, all-linear constraints, integrality confined to $y, r, u, c$. Solvable by branch-and-bound / branch-and-cut (Gurobi, CPLEX, SCIP).

**Key modeling choices:**
- **Big-M disjunctions** encode ordering, rerouting, and "pass before/after disruption" logic without nonlinearity.
- **Speed-level binaries $u_{t,e,k}$** discretize the speed profile, keeping the running-time coupling (4) and energy (24) piecewise-linear.
- **Rerouting binaries $r_{t,e}$** enable local diversion to the opposite track during the disruption window, with (16)–(17) guaranteeing conflict-free bidirectional operation on the shared track.
- **Cancellation $c_t$** removes a train via big-M zeroing, penalized in the objective and capped by (29).

**Assumptions (marked):**
1. *(Assumption)* Speed is discretized into a finite set of levels $K$; energy is a piecewise-linear function of speed.
2. *(Assumption)* Only affected trains ($T^{aff}$) may be cancelled or rerouted.
3. *(Assumption)* No overtaking on open track (order consistency enforced via $y$).
4. *(Assumption)* Big-M is a tight bound on the planning horizon.
5. *(Assumption)* Disruption blocks one track direction on segments $E^{dis}$ during $[t_{start}, t_{end}]$.

# Integrated Train Rescheduling and Speed Management Problem (TRSMP) — MILP Formulation

Below is the complete linear model derived from the generated code. All assumptions are marked explicitly.

---

## Assumptions

1. **(A1) Discretized speed levels.** Speed is chosen from a finite set `K` with known values `v_k`. This linearizes the nonlinear running-time relation `u = L/v`.
2. **(A2) Discretized positions.** The set `P` is used only for acceleration/deceleration checks; acceleration between consecutive segments is approximated using the average speed of each segment.
3. **(A3) Direction encoding.** `d_i ∈ {+1, −1}` (up/down). Same-direction trains share a track; opposite-direction trains normally use different tracks, but rerouting (`y=1`) forces them onto the same track.
4. **(A4) Affected indicator.** A train is "affected" if its *scheduled* arrival at a blocked segment falls inside the disruption window `W`. This is a parameter (not a variable), a standard linearization of the disjunctive condition.
5. **(A5) Cancellation.** If `z[i,s]=1`, the train is cancelled from segment `s` onward (downstream times set to 0), enforced with big-M.
6. **(A6) Ordering antisymmetry.** Defined only for pairs of same-direction trains on the same segment.
7. **(A7) Acceleration/deceleration.** Approximated as `(v_{i,s+1} − v_{i,s}) / u_{i,s} ∈ [−b_max, a_max]`, with `v_{i,s}` linearized via the speed-level binaries.
8. **(A8) Objective.** Delay is measured at arrival times; energy is `Σ E_k · L_s · v[i,s,k]`.
9. **(A9) Big-M.** `M` is chosen large enough to deactivate constraints (e.g., 10× the horizon).
10. **(A10) Time window `W`.** Encoded as a binary indicator `affected[i,s]` computed from scheduled times.

---

## Sets and Indices

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `T` | Set of trains, indexed by `i, j` |
| `S` | Set of stations, indexed by `s = 1..|S|` |
| `SEG` | Set of segments, `s` connects station `s` and `s+1` |
| `K` | Set of discrete speed levels, indexed by `k` |
| `P` | Set of discretized positions, indexed by `p` |
| `PAIRS` | Set of train pairs `(i,j)` with `i < j` |
| `B ⊆ SEG` | Set of blocked segments (disruption area) |
| `W = [t_start, t_end]` | Disruption time window |

---

## Parameters

| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `L_s` | Length of segment `s` |
| `v_k` | Speed value of level `k` |
| `E_k` | Energy consumption rate at speed level `k` |
| `v_max` | Maximum allowable speed |
| `a_max`, `b_max` | Maximum acceleration / deceleration |
| `d_min` | Minimum headway (same direction, same track) |
| `δ` | Minimum separation for opposite-direction trains sharing a track |
| `t_dwell_min`, `t_dwell_max` | Min/max dwell time |
| `t_run_min_s`, `t_run_max_s` | Min/max running time on segment `s` |
| `w_delay`, `w_energy` | Objective weights |
| `t_sched_arr[i,s]`, `t_sched_dep[i,s]` | Scheduled arrival/departure times |
| `affected[i,s]` | Binary indicator: train `i` affected on segment `s` |
| `M` | Large constant (big-M) |

---

## Decision Variables

| Variable | Domain | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `t_arr[i,s]` | `≥ 0` | Actual arrival time of train `i` at station `s` |
| `t_dep[i,s]` | `≥ 0` | Actual departure time of train `i` from station `s` |
| `u[i,s]` | `≥ 0` | Running time of train `i` on segment `s` |
| `x[i,j,s]` | `{0,1}` | 1 if train `i` precedes train `j` on segment `s` |
| `y[i,s]` | `{0,1}` | 1 if train `i` is rerouted to the opposite track on segment `s` |
| `v[i,s,k]` | `{0,1}` | 1 if train `i` uses speed level `k` on segment `s` |
| `z[i,s]` | `{0,1}` | 1 if train `i` is cancelled on segment `s` |

---

## Objective Function

Minimize total weighted delay plus energy consumption:

```
min  w_delay · Σ_{i∈T} Σ_{s∈S} ( t_arr[i,s] − t_sched_arr[i,s] )
   + w_energy · Σ_{i∈T} Σ_{s∈SEG} Σ_{k∈K} E_k · L_s · v[i,s,k]
```

---

## Constraints

**(1) Arrival/departure propagation** — for all `i ∈ T`, `s ∈ SEG` with `s < |S|`:
```
t_arr[i, s+1] = t_dep[i, s] + u[i, s]
```

**(2) Dwell time bounds** — for all `i ∈ T`, `s ∈ S`:
```
t_dep[i,s] − t_arr[i,s] ≥ t_dwell_min
t_dep[i,s] − t_arr[i,s] ≤ t_dwell_max
```

**(3) Running time linked to speed profile** — for all `i ∈ T`, `s ∈ SEG`:
```
u[i,s] = Σ_{k∈K} ( L_s / v_k ) · v[i,s,k]
```

**(4) Exactly one speed level per train per segment** — for all `i ∈ T`, `s ∈ SEG`:
```
Σ_{k∈K} v[i,s,k] = 1
```

**(5) Speed level bounds** — for all `i ∈ T`, `s ∈ SEG`, `k ∈ K`:
```
v[i,s,k] · v_k ≤ v_max
```

**(6) Ordering constraints (same direction, same track)** — for all `(i,j) ∈ PAIRS`, `s ∈ SEG` with `d_i = d_j`:
```
t_dep[j,s] ≥ t_arr[i,s] + d_min − M · ( 1 − x[i,j,s] )
```

**(7) Ordering antisymmetry** — for all `(i,j) ∈ PAIRS`, `s ∈ SEG` with `d_i = d_j`:
```
x[i,j,s] + x[j,i,s] = 1
```

**(8) Rerouting only allowed on blocked segments** — for all `i ∈ T`, `s ∈ SEG` with `s ∉ B`:
```
y[i,s] = 0
```

**(9) Rerouting conflict (opposite directions sharing track)** — for all `(i,j) ∈ PAIRS`, `s ∈ SEG` with `d_i ≠ d_j`:
```
t_dep[j,s] ≥ t_arr[i,s] + δ − M·(1 − y[i,s]) − M·(1 − y[j,s])
```

**(10) Disruption blockage** — for all `i ∈ T`, `s ∈ SEG` with `affected[i,s] = 1`:
```
y[i,s] + z[i,s] ≥ 1
```

**(11) Cancellation** — for all `i ∈ T`, `s ∈ S`, `k ∈ K`:
```
t_arr[i,s] ≤ M · ( 1 − z[i,s] )
t_dep[i,s] ≤ M · ( 1 − z[i,s] )
v[i,s,k]   ≤ 1 − z[i,s]
```

**(12) Acceleration / deceleration limits** — for all `i ∈ T`, `s ∈ SEG` with `s < |SEG|`:
```
Σ_k v_k · v[i,s+1,k] − Σ_k v_k · v[i,s,k] ≤ a_max · u[i,s]
Σ_k v_k · v[i,s,k] − Σ_k v_k · v[i,s+1,k] ≤ b_max · u[i,s]
```

**(13) Domains:**
```
t_arr[i,s], t_dep[i,s], u[i,s] ≥ 0
x[i,j,s], y[i,s], v[i,s,k], z[i,s] ∈ {0,1}
```

---

## Summary Table

| # | Constraint | Form |
|---|-----------|------|
| 1 | Propagation | `t_arr[i,s+1] = t_dep[i,s] + u[i,s]` |
| 2 | Dwell | `t_dwell_min ≤ t_dep − t_arr ≤ t_dwell_max` |
| 3 | Running time | `u[i,s] = Σ_k (L_s/v_k) v[i,s,k]` |
| 4 | One speed | `Σ_k v[i,s,k] = 1` |
| 5 | Speed bound | `v_k ≤ v_max` |
| 6 | Ordering | `t_dep[j,s] ≥ t_arr[i,s] + d_min − M(1−x[i,j,s])` |
| 7 | Antisymmetry | `x[i,j,s] + x[j,i,s] = 1` |
| 8 | Reroute only in B | `y[i,s] = 0` if `s ∉ B` |
| 9 | Reroute conflict | `t_dep[j,s] ≥ t_arr[i,s] + δ − M(1−y[i,s]) − M(1−y[j,s])` |
| 10 | Blockage | `y[i,s] + z[i,s] ≥ 1` if affected |
| 11 | Cancellation | `t_arr, t_dep ≤ M(1−z)`, `v ≤ 1−z` |
| 12 | Accel/decel | `−b_max·u ≤ Δv ≤ a_max·u` |
| 13 | Domains | `t,u ≥ 0`; `x,y,v,z ∈ {0,1}` |

**Objective:** `min Σ w_delay·(t_arr − t_sched_arr) + w_energy·Σ E_k·L_s·v[i,s,k]`

All nonlinearities (running time, acceleration) are linearized via the discrete speed-level binaries `v[i,s,k]`, yielding a pure MILP that simultaneously optimizes train times, orders, routes, and speed profiles while producing a conflict-free timetable.
